newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil and fuel firmer.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil and fuel firmer.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday.
Gasoline was steady with premium unleaded cargoes at $233/$234 cif, and fob $10 lower.
"The Med is pretty balanced as far as 95 and above (grades)," said one trader. "Below 95, the low run is in a bit of a surplus."
She said demand for cat gas from Turkey and Nigeria had dropped off, hurting prices.
The arb to the U.S. and NWE is shut, she said.
Naphtha was steady to higher after a sharp rally in crude prices, with cargoes up $3 at $222/$225 cif. Traders awaited the 1997 Egypt tender results.
Gas oil firmed on stronger futures but despite active enquiries and adequate availability of vessels bids and offers remained far apart and trade was quiet.
"People are offering numbers that are too high to get people to really move," a trader said.
A cargo of Italian 0.2 percent heating oil was offered into Greece at cif high +$3 and a cargo of French heating oil was offered at cif high +$2 but neither aroused a response.
Traders described the market as potentially strong because of talk of another Turkish tender for four cargoes for December.

Fuel oil activity was centred on low sulphur cracked. The main Med buyer was understood to be discreetly trying to pick up material in a rising market. Prices were assessed in the mid $130s cif Italy after two wet deals yesterday for upwards of 90,000 tonnes. Traders said only one 45-50,000 tonne cargo was available this month with the seller looking for around $128 fob NWE. Tonnage has become tight with freight now put around $9 a tonne on 50,000 tonners heading into the Med from the North.
High sulphur cracked fuel was quiet and prices steady.
